The later two add words not in the Russian to carry the relation. Tolstoy himself says вы and its dictionary equivalent vous differ in coldness. A documented instance of the compensation mechanism; the evidence on what readers recover is translators' and the author's, not readers'. | Active |
| [CASE-067](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-067.md) | The reception of Deborah Smith's The Vegetarian: the Booker judges' task, the Korean critics' task, and one critic's two verdicts | Deborah Smith's English version of Han Kang's 채식주의자 won the 2016 Man Booker International Prize, while Korean critics published lists of errors and charged it with embellishment. Each side's task is stated in print: the judges evaluate "the finished English-language work on their own terms", while assessment in Korea "does usually involve comparison". Charse Yun perceives what both sides perceive and gives two verdicts by changing task. Part of the split is access, not weight: some errors are invisible to readers without Korean. | Active |
| [CASE-068](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-068.md) | Risk messages passed down diffusion chains: the evaluative signal kept and amplified while the content decays (Moussaïd, Brighton and Gaissmaier; Jagiello and Hills) | In two serial-reproduction experiments on risk messages, each link's message was coded for content and, on a separate scheme, for the evaluative stance of its statements toward the hazard. Content got shorter, less accurate and more divergent; the evaluative signal survived and drifted negative, and re-exposure to the balanced source did not undo the drift. The transmitters' own risk perception, measured by questionnaire, predicts the direction of the change. Documented chain evidence for evaluative stance; none for footing. | Active |
| [CASE-069](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-069.md) | Labov's recorded sounding sessions: ritual insult turning personal, with the same exchange shape and a different act | Labov's team taped sounding among Harlem peer groups. Boot answers David's taunt with a remark "related to A-5 in exactly the way that one sound is related to another", yet both are taken as personal insults: denied, objected to, wept over. Labov's rule puts the difference in a further relation, the shared knowledge before an audience that the proposition is untrue. A documented, non-institutional case for [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) in which the act follows a relation among the parties, and for [CLAIM-138](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-138.md), since the exchange relations alone match and the acts still differ. | Active |
| [CASE-070](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-070.md) | Voita, Sennrich and Titov's BLEU-tied translation systems that differ on keeping ты or вы across sentences | Two English-to-Russian subtitle translation systems score the same BLEU (32.40 and 32.38, not significantly different). On a contrastive test built from held-out films, which asks whether a system keeps the T or V form of "you" consistent across sentences, one is at chance (50.0%) and the other is right in 81.6% of cases. A documented instance, on a pragmatic distinction, of two realizations equal under a standard probe family and different under an independently built one. An ML paper that neither record holds. | Active |
| [CASE-071](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-071.md) | Kovacs, Deutsch and Freitag's metric bias in MBR decoding: translations a metric selects, that the metric and its neighbours rate better and human raters do not | Minimum Bayes risk and quality-estimation decoding pick, from 128 sampled translations, the one a neural metric scores best. That metric and other neural metrics rate the picks significantly better than greedy decoding; human MQM raters find them no better, and for four system and language-pair combinations significantly worse. [CASE-041](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-041.md)'s result in text, by selection rather than training. The distinction lost is accuracy, not a pragmatic one; a stipulated English-to-Russian ты/вы variant states the design that would make it pragmatic. | Active |
| [CASE-072](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-072.md) | Hafez's "Shirazi Turk" in English: one ungendered beloved rendered as a maid, as God and as a boy | The opening of Hafez's ghazal 3 names a beloved, "that Shirazi Turk", whose sex and nature the Persian leaves open. English forces a choice at the first possessive. Jones (1771) and Bell (1897) make the beloved a maid, Clarke (1891) makes it God, and Davis (2012) makes it a boy, and Davis says in print that his choice is arbitrary. A documented instance of the half of a change of cover in which the rendering decides what the source left open. The disagreement on the source is among translators and scholars; no reader agreement has been measured. | Active |
| [CASE-073](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-073.md) | The Kia Provo: one concept-car name, a blank coinage to the motor press and taken as honouring the IRA in Northern Ireland | In March 2013 Kia showed a concept car at Geneva named the Provo, "from the word 'provoke'". The motor press found no meaning in the name; in Northern Ireland, where "Provo" names a member of the Provisional IRA, six MPs said it "has caused deep offence". Kia said it meant no offence, and withdrew the name for the UK and Ireland. One name, the speaker's intention fixed and declared, a new audience, and an unintended reading taken up and acted on: the accidental, verbal variant of [CASE-064](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-064.md), illustrating [CLAIM-224](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-224.md). | Active |
| [CASE-074](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-074.md) | Twitch Plays Pokémon in democracy mode, with the running tally shown while the votes come in | The crowd of [CASE-075](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-075.md) in democracy mode. Each move is the button that collects the most votes in a short window, and the running tally is shown while the votes arrive, so the current majority can sway the votes still coming. The owner judges it a better demonstration of a population with drift-diffusion decision dynamics than anarchy mode. Showing the tally adds feedback, and feedback moves the dynamics toward winner-take-all. | Active |
| [CASE-075](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-075.md) | Twitch Plays Pokémon in anarchy mode: one avatar steered through the map by the running aggregate of a crowd's inputs | In February 2014 a stream let everyone in its chat play one copy of Pokémon Red at once, with every typed button press executed in turn. The owner offers its navigation as a working approximation of an agent made of a population whose decisions follow drift-diffusion dynamics. The crowd's direction reorganizes continuously and is not switched. The record holds no source for the case yet. | Active |
| [CASE-076](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-076.md) | Twin pattern-keepers: two systems keep the same pattern, one by its own responses and one through an external controller, and only removing the controller tells them apart | A10 §3.3's paired design, the case behind [QUESTION-086](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-086.md). Matching behaviour and persistence, different organization. Removing the controller destroys one system's pattern and not the other's. A10 then made it harder: the internal regulator at one scale is supported by other processes at another, so which side of the boundary the controller sits on depends on where the boundary is drawn. | Active |
| [CASE-077](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-077.md) | The reciprocal pair: two processes that endorse only each other under recursive delegation, so that each one's authority returns to it through the other | A2 §5's counterexample to the ban on self-endorsement: "Suppose D1 endorses D2, and D2 endorses D1." Under g = (1 − η)b + ηEᵀg, each operator's authority comes partly from its own endorsement returned after two hops. It came back in A6 as authority that "may circulate". Used to show that a ban on self-endorsement does not make authority independent of one's own endorsements. | Active |
| [CASE-078](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-078.md) | Who keeps placing on r/place: the proposed survival analysis of the released placement logs, testing whether participants return while their art survives and whether unaffiliated placement cools | Proposed by the owner on 2026-10-13, not run. On the released 2017, 2022 and 2023 logs, model each participant's hazard of stopping, with the survival of the art they placed into as a time-varying covariate, and estimate the rate of placements that fit no artwork over the event. The main threat is reverse causality: persistent defenders keep their art alive. So the design leans on destruction the participant did not cause, such as the 2022 moderator wipes and large raids. It is the test named in [CLAIM-274](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-274.md)'s defeater. | Active |
| [CASE-079](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-079.md) | r/place: a shared pixel canvas on which each Reddit user could place one pixel at a time under a cooldown, and communities coordinated off the canvas to build, defend and overwrite images | The owner proposed it at U8 of the 2026-10-13 exchange: "every user can modify a single pixel once, and different subreddits coordinated to present certain images or even warred amongst each other over regions of the canvas". Reddit ran it in 2017, 2022 and 2023, and released the 2022 placement log. A8 read it as the exchange's two canvases made visible: the pixels as the meaning canvas, the plans, templates and alliances off the canvas as the influence canvas. First time the thing turns up in the record. The event and the data are documented. The readings of them are proposals. | Active |
| [CASE-080](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-080.md) | The skeptic who delegates: a critic that cannot overturn an emerging consensus gives its authority to a process that can generate alternatives | A3 §6's worked example. Four processes: an integrator and a decision- maker push toward a decision, a skeptic disagrees, and a generator can translate neglected evidence into new hypotheses. The skeptic does not try to win. It endorses the generator, whose hypotheses change the decision landscape. Used to show delegation as a route to one's goals, and dissent made useful by a role. | Active |
| [CASE-081](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-081.md) | Self-maintenance learned for a designer's reward: a system that maintains itself because it was trained to, and later revises the policy and keeps maintaining itself without further instruction | A10 §6.1's boundary case, "a system that learns to maintain itself only because an external designer rewards that behavior", with its question whether the maintenance becomes endogenous "once the system can revise the policy and maintain the associated governance without continued external instruction". It is the case [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md) is about, and the place where that objection could be answered. | Active |
